title: The drunkard's reach
hook: Walk randomly 4 times longer. Do you get 4 times farther?

knows: that molecules in a gas or liquid move randomly
doesNotKnow: that typical distance in a random walk grows as the square root of the number of steps, so spreading slows

misconception: Diffusion is steady travel, so 4 times longer means 4 times farther.
objective: The learner can explain that random steps partly cancel, so the typical distance grows as √N: 4 times as many steps reach about 2 times as far, which is why diffusion is fast at short range and slow at long range.

claims.text: For a random walk, the typical (root-mean-square) distance from the start grows as the square root of the number of steps.
claims.source: RMS displacement = step × √N (Berg, Random Walks in Biology, ch. 1).

claims.text: 4 times as many steps gives about 2 times the typical distance: √100 ÷ √25 = 10 ÷ 5 = 2.
In the stage's cloud of 40 walkers the typical distance goes from about 4.9 step lengths at 25 steps to about 9.5 at 100 steps, about 1.9 times.
claims.source: mulberry32 seed 1, untuned (the first seed tried); unit steps in a uniform random direction. Node script: rms(25) = 4.93, rms(100) = 9.54, ratio 1.93. Across seeds 1–500 with 40 walkers the ratio has median 2.01 and 90% range 1.70–2.36.

claims.text: To go twice as far by random motion takes about four times as long; this is how molecules diffuse.
claims.source: Diffusion distance ∝ √(Dt) (Atkins, Physical Chemistry, 'diffusion'; Berg, Random Walks in Biology).

claims.text: Stage: the ring is the root-mean-square distance of the 40 walkers; each step is 1 unit in a random direction.

recall.question: A smell spreads 1 m through still air in about 1 minute by diffusion alone. To spread 3 m it takes about…
recall.why: Distance grows as the square root of time, so 3 times as far takes 3² = 9 times as long.
